page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-64 is a flexible compute instance powered by the Ampere-1 processor from the AmpereOne family, built on 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring single-threaded predictability per vCPU. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per dedicated vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent throughput in multithreaded and memory-bound tasks alongside moderate single-core computational limits. Single-core stress-ng tests recorded 572.99, placing in the lower decile, while Geekbench single-core scored 1088.0. Multi-core execution demonstrates balanced scaling, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5860.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 10867.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 53.27 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 71.2 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing cached block read speeds of 703.3 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks align in the average tier, with Redis sustaining 11.3 million SET operations per second and static web serving reaching 12.25 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-64 configuration maximizes memory capacity relative to compute footprint, making it cost-effective for memory-constrained services that do not require high single-thread clock frequencies. However, applications requiring x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 or high-throughput machine learning inference are constrained by the Arm64 architecture and moderate vector performance. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, static and dynamic web backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-64 provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz on the 64-bit Ampere-1 Arm64 architecture. Equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, it offers an elevated 8 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning it with memory-intensive compute requirements. The instance omits integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for disk operations. Benchmark data reveals modest single-thread compute capabilities alongside reliable multi-core and memory throughput, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5860.0 and Redis performance of 11.3 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 53.27 GB/sec for uncached reads and 71.2 GB/sec for uncached writes. While unsuitable for vector-heavy workloads or low-latency machine learning inference, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-64 functions effectively for Redis instances, in-memory caches, software compilation servers, and general web infrastructure.
